newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset sees net ad sales up 6 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset sees net ad sales up 6 pct in 1996.

text.p: Italian TV and advertising group Mediaset SpA said it sees its net advertising sales rising 6 percent in the whole of 1996, after the company had seen gross advertising sales rise some 6.2 percent during the first half of 1996.
These figures were given at an analysts' meeting in London this morning with the presentation led by group chairman Fedele Confalonieri and managing director Ubaldo Livolsi.
In the first half of 1996, net sales in the whole Mediaset group, of which its advertising arm Publitalia accounts for 90 percent, rose some 3.7 percent.
Gross sales include those sales made with other divisions in the Mediaset group, for example with its TV stations.
One analyst who was at the meeting expects total group sales to rise by more than 5.5 percent in 1996, but Mediaset has not given any indication of group sales forecasts for 1996.

Other analysts were not so positive and some of them believed that net profits for 1996 would show a small fall to around 490 billion lire. In 1995, Mediaset showed net profits of 497 billion lire on sales of 1.66 trillion lire.

Analysts said the biggest uncertainty overhanging the stock is draft legislation aimed at controlling advertising and market shares in the Italian TV market. But analysts said that Mediaset was confident at the meeting that the draft legislation would be revised before becoming law.
